Ni50Ti44xAl6Mox (x=0, 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 3) alloys were prepared by arc melting, using high purity Ni, Ti, Al and Mo elements under Ar atmosphere. The ingots were turned over and remelted at least four times
Homogenization was performed in vacuum at 1 000 °C for 6 h followed by air-cooling.

Homogenization was performed in vacuum at 1 000 °C for 6 h followed by air-cooling.
It is seen from Fig.1(a) that the Ni50Ti44Al6 alloy is composed of dual phases, a predominant phase (grey) and a second phase (black) along grain boundary
the second phase is Ti2Ni with a volume fraction less than 5%
Similar morphology can be found in Ni50Ti43Al6Mo1 alloy as shown in Fig.1(b).
for Ni50Ti43Al6Mo1 alloy, the intensity of Ti2Ni phase peak is enhanced compared to Ni50Ti44Al6 alloy, meaning the increased volume fraction of it.
The larger particle A (mean diameter is about 150 nm) is determined as 71.06Mo-21.31Ti-7.63Ni (at%) in composition
Some Ti2Ni particles have also been found within NiTi phase as shown in Fig.2(b) (see Table 1 for its composition), whose size ranges from 200 nm to 500 nm.
when Mo content reaches 3 at%, some blocky white precipitates appear as shown in Fig.1(d). The white precipitates have been proved to be a Mo-rich phase by EDS using SEM

The specific strengths of Ni50Ti43Al6Mo1 alloy are 305 MPa/(g·cm3) at room temperature
It is seen that the maximum of σ0.2 at 600 °C is 940 MPa for Ni50Ti43Al6Mo1 alloy
and 153 MPa/(g·cm3) at 600 °C, higher than that of Ti-48Al alloy at respective temperature
the change of mechanical properties should be mainly attributed to the solid solution hardening of Mo.
besides the effect of solid solution hardening, the precipitation strengthening of Moss should be another reason for the increase of HV and σ0.2 and the decrease of plasticity at room temperature.
the predominant phase is NiTi containing a small amount of Al and the second phase is Ti2Ni
